messages:
maria_sales: hey team - customer wants a private deploy POC but their security requires preserving client source IPs for downstream onprem firewalls. they asked if PrivateLink preserves srcip or if we need BYOIP/EIP. any quick guidance?

raj_neteng: short answer: PrivateLink (interface endpoints) -> source IP will appear as the ENI/NAT IP in the customer VPC. it does NOT preserve the original client public IP to the service backend. :point_up:

anna_se: +1. most customers expecting 1:1 client IP preservation are surprised. common patterns:
- BYOIP/EIP + static egress from our side so customer can allow a fixed set of IPs
- have customer terminate TLS/proxy in their VPC and forward X-Forwarded-For to the private service (app-layer)
- use a TCP proxy with PROXY protocol (NLB -> our backend) to pass client IP at transport layer

leo_solutions: for POC constraints: if they control the firewall allowlist only, BYOIP or reserved EIPs are simplest for handoff. but call out costs: EIPs + NATGW bandwidth.

maria_sales: ok noted. they also asked about sticky sessions (session affinity) for long-running streaming inference calls. does PrivateLink change that?

raj_neteng: PrivateLink is just the connectivity. session affinity depends on the fronting load balancer/NGINX/proxy. if you use NLB with TLS passthrough + source IP hashing, you can get connection-based affinity. if you terminate TLS on LB and use cookie affinity, that's app-level. streaming tends to prefer TCP-level affinity.

anna_se: recommendation for Redwood Private:
1) If customer needs true client-srcip on their firewall for auditing, do BYOIP/EIP on our egress and share the EIP list to allowlist (fastest to validate).
2) If they need original client ip at the application layer, use PROXY protocol or X-Forwarded-For from their proxy (requires app change).
3) For streaming affinity, use NLB + long-lived TCP connections or sticky flow hash. test with your typical request_size/latency.

maria_sales: they asked for a minimal firewall snippet to show security team what to allow. can you drop a sample?

raj_neteng: sure — example for allowing our reserved EIPs and PrivateLink endpoint connections: 
```
# Allow Redwood Private egress IPs to reach onprem firewall (HTTPS + streaming)
allow from 203.0.113.12/32 to <ONPREM_PUBLIC_IP> port 443 proto tcp
allow from 203.0.113.13/32 to <ONPREM_PUBLIC_IP> port 443 proto tcp
# If using proxy protocol or tcp health checks, allow port 10256 (example)
allow from 203.0.113.12/32 to <ONPREM_PUBLIC_IP> port 10256 proto tcp
```
Replace with the actual EIPs we give them. also call out that traffic traversing PrivateLink will appear from the interface endpoint ENI CIDR in their VPC (you can show route tables).

leo_solutions: another design we propose in the handoff doc: give them 2 options and cost/ops tradeoffs:
- Option A (fast, lower dev): BYOIP / reserved EIPs from Redwood, we egress from those IPs. Tradeoffs: NAT/EIP cost, capacity planning, limited IPs to share.
- Option B (customer-managed preservation): customer runs an NLB/proxy in their VPC that terminates/forwards and includes original client headers or PROXY protocol. Tradeoffs: requires app change, supports richer auditing, preserves true client ip.

maria_sales: can we provide a short bullet list for the security questionnaire (Q: does PrivateLink preserve client IP?)

anna_se: yes — suggested answers: 
- Q: Will client source IPs be preserved across PrivateLink?
  A: No — AWS Interface Endpoints present traffic from endpoint ENIs; original public client IP will not reach the service backend unchanged.
- Q: How can we support allowlisting?
  A: We can supply a stable list of egress IPs (BYOIP/EIP) for firewall allowlisting or recommend a proxy pattern using PROXY protocol/X-Forwarded-For.
- Q: Any limitations for streaming?
  A: Streaming is supported; ensure TCP-level connection affinity (NLB) or app-level session tokens to maintain state.

maria_sales: perfect. they want estimated costs for Option A (BYOIP + NATGW). any ballpark numbers to put in the proposal?

leo_solutions: rough: per-month per-EIP negligible but NATGW/data processing is the main cost. plan for NATGW (~$30-$40/month per AZ) + data transfer out costs depending on region. also extra ops for maintaining reserved IPs. include burst capacity if POC will load test.

raj_neteng: add a note: if they require thousands of distinct client ip addresses for per-user firewalling, that's not feasible. recommend token-based auth or app-level identity instead.

maria_sales: OK I'll draft the handoff to their security and include the sample firewall snippet + two-option matrix and the cost caveats. tagging @leo_solutions and @raj_neteng for final sign-off before I send. :pray:

leo_solutions: lgtm from solutioning perspective. one more: include instructions for how we rotate EIPs and notification cadence — security teams ask this.

raj_neteng: i'll add a one-paragraph on rotation & outage fallback: we keep N backup EIPs, update allowlist, and fail over to a compatible model in another region if capacity constrained. coordinate >72h window for planned rotation.

deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled: private-poc-network-docs -> staging (runbook-id: pr-759).

maria_sales: thanks everyone — i'll send the doc to the customer today and post the final thread here with attachments.

anna_se: cheers. :tada:
